subject: Moonlake Insurance — backup customer reference (EU data residency / anonymized option)
body:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Petrova <elena.petrova@moonlakeinsurance.eu>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Jun 14, 2025 at 09:12 AM GMT+2
Subject: Moonlake Insurance — backup customer reference (EU data residency / anonymized option)

Hi Elena,

Hope you’re doing well.

We’re standing up a small customer reference program on our side (case studies + scheduled reference calls for qualified prospects). Given your team’s work with Redwood so far, I wanted to ask whether Moonlake would be open to participating as a *backup* reference candidate for EMEA.

Two options (and we can keep this very conservative):

1) Reference calls only (private):
- 1:1 calls with qualified prospects, scheduled and hosted by Redwood
- you control topics + who attends on your side
- no recordings

2) An anonymized write-up (public, optional):
- e.g., “EU insurance provider” / “regulated insurer in DACH”
- no logo, no customer name, no employee names
- we can keep architecture details high-level and avoid any sensitive deployment specifics

I know you’ve flagged data residency and publicity constraints previously. If the public option is a non-starter, the “reference-call-only” path is still valuable for us.

Would you be open to a quick 20 min chat next week to confirm what’s acceptable (and what’s not), and what approvals you’d need internally?

Thanks,
Hannah

—
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, EMEA
Redwood Inference


From: Elena Petrova <elena.petrova@moonlakeinsurance.eu>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jun 16, 2025 at 11:03 AM GMT+2
Subject: Re: Moonlake Insurance — backup customer reference (EU data residency / anonymized option)

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for reaching out and for laying out the options clearly.

In principle, we can help, but we have strict constraints:

- Public case study: likely not possible with our name/logo, and we generally avoid public vendor endorsements.
- Even anonymized: may be possible, but we’d need legal + comms review and we would not be able to include identifiable details.
- Reference calls: potentially yes, if the prospect is a regulated/enterprise buyer and the call is controlled (agenda in advance, no recording, no screenshots/shared dashboards).
- Data residency is non-negotiable for us (EU-only processing). We also need to avoid any discussion that implies otherwise.

If it helps, our Legal/Comms contact for anything external-facing is Dieter Weber (cc’ing him here).

Best,
Elena

Elena Petrova
Head of Platform Engineering
Moonlake Insurance


From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Petrova <elena.petrova@moonlakeinsurance.eu>
Cc: Dieter Weber <dieter.weber@moonlakeinsurance.eu>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jun 16, 2025 at 02:28 PM GMT+2
Subject: Re: Moonlake Insurance — backup customer reference (EU data residency / anonymized option)

Elena (and hi Dieter),

This is very helpful — thank you.

Given what you shared, I suggest we focus on “reference calls only” as the primary path, and treat the anonymized write-up as optional / later.

How Redwood typically runs the private reference calls:
- Redwood schedules + moderates; we’ll share agenda + attendee list ahead of time
- we can keep the call to 30 minutes and avoid any screensharing
- we’ll prep the prospect with explicit boundaries (no questions on your internal security posture, vendors, customer data, etc.)
- absolutely no recording

On EU-only: fully understood, and we will keep that as a hard boundary in any reference discussion.

Attaching two docs for context:
- Redwood_Customer_Reference_Program_Overview.pdf (high level overview; no commitments implied)
- Customer_Quote_Logo_Release_Form_Template.docx (FYI only — this is for *public* assets; we wouldn’t push this if you prefer reference-only)

If you’re open to it, could we do a short alignment call this week with you + Dieter + my CS counterpart (Rachel) to confirm:
1) whether Moonlake is comfortable being a private reference (EMEA)
2) the criteria for which prospects qualify
3) frequency (e.g., max calls per quarter)
4) any words/phrasing we should avoid (especially around residency)

I’m free Wed 10:00–12:00 CET or Thu 15:00–17:00 CET.

Best,
Hannah

—
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, EMEA
Redwood Inference


From: Dieter Weber <dieter.weber@moonlakeinsurance.eu>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Petrova <elena.petrova@moonlakeinsurance.eu>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 17, 2025 at 04:48 PM GMT+2
Subject: Re: Moonlake Insurance — backup customer reference (EU data residency / anonymized option)

Hannah,

Thank you for the materials.

We can consider participation under the following conditions:

A) Publicity / written material
- No company name, no logo, no employee names/titles, no photos.
- No exact performance metrics or cost figures. If necessary, only broad ranges (e.g., “double-digit percentage improvement”) and only after review.
- Any written content must be submitted for review/approval prior to publication.

B) Reference calls (private)
- Maximum: 2 calls per calendar quarter.
- Duration: 30 minutes.
- Redwood to provide agenda and attendee list (names + company) at least 48 hours in advance.
- No recording. No screenshots. No sharing of dashboards.
- We will not sign NDAs directly with third-party prospects. The call must be moderated by Redwood and treated as confidential.
- We reserve the right to decline a call based on the prospect or topic.

C) Data residency
- Please avoid any statements that imply cross-border processing. Our position is “EU-only.”

If these constraints work for you, we can proceed to schedule an alignment call. Thursday 15:30 CET works.

Regards,
Dieter Weber
Legal Counsel (Commercial)
Moonlake Insurance
